title: Constructible devissage: the thick-subcategory generation
statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type scheme over $k$ and $A$ a
finite coefficient ring as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions].
The triangulated category $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ is the thick subcategory of
$D(X,A)$ generated by the objects

$$
Rg_*j_!L ,
$$

where $U$ is a locally closed stratum of $X$,
$j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ is the open immersion into its closure,
$g:\overline U\hookrightarrow X$ is the closed immersion, and $L$ is a lisse
sheaf of $A$-modules on $U$ with flat stalks. Constant coefficients
$L=A_U$ do not suffice in general.

proof.text: First work on the small étale site. Write $\mathcal H_{\Et}$ for the thick subcategory generated by the indicated $Rg_*j_!L$. The scheme $X$ is Noetherian: $\Spec k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, and its spectrum has one point), and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies to its finite-type structure morphism. The same holds for its locally closed subschemes. The ring $A$ is finite and commutative by the coefficient conventions. The empty scheme causes no exception: its sheaf category is zero and the generated thick subcategory is zero.

source.place: Proof, Steps 0–2: setting for the flat-model and stratification argument

proof.text: The two descriptions of the allowed lisse coefficients agree: flat finite stalks are precisely finite projective local models. Indeed a finite $A$-module $M$ has a finite presentation: choose a finite surjection $A^r\twoheadrightarrow M$; its kernel is a finite set because $A^r$ is finite, hence has a finite generating set. If $M$ is flat, [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] makes it projective. Conversely projective modules are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. A lisse sheaf is locally a constant finite module, so this calculation applies to each local model and its stalks. In particular a lisse sheaf with flat stalks is flat as a sheaf: on a trivializing étale cover its tensor functor is the tensor functor with the flat local model, and exactness can be checked on that cover.

For a locally closed immersion $a:U\hookrightarrow X$, use its factorization $a=g\circ j$ through its closure. The locally closed extension $a_!L$ in [lem-fin-constructible-devissage] is $g_*j_!L$. By [lem-fin-closed-immersion], $R g_*j_!L=g_*j_!L$: $j_!L$ is constructible by [lem-fin-extension-by-zero], and higher closed direct images vanish. Thus the generator family agrees with the locally closed $a_!L$ family in [det-sf-flat-model-generation], using Step 2 to identify the coefficient condition. Clause (3) of that existing node says that $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ is thick and contains those $a_!L$. Consequently every indicated generator is in $D^b_{ctf}$, and $\mathcal H_{\Et}\subseteq D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$. This uses only immersion cases and the existing flat-model lemma, not an aggregate six-functor stability theorem.

Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$. Choose integers $a\leq b$ bounding its Tor amplitude. Apply [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] on the Noetherian scheme $X$ with the finite ring $A$: it supplies a bounded complex $P$, zero outside $[a,b]$, whose terms are flat constructible sheaves and whose derived image is isomorphic to $K$. No assertion is made about finite Tor amplitude of the individual cohomology sheaves of $K$.

Each term $F=P^q$ belongs to $\mathcal H_{\Et}$. Clauses (1) and (2) of [det-sf-flat-model-generation] give an ordered finite stratification with $L_r=F|_{S_r}$ finite projective lisse and a finite extension filtration of $F$ with factors $a_{r!}L_r$. By Step 3 these factors are the indicated generators. Regard each short exact sequence in the filtration as a short exact sequence of complexes concentrated in degree zero; [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] makes it a distinguished triangle. Induction on the number of filtration factors, starting at $0$, and the defining cone closure of a thick subcategory put $F$ in $\mathcal H_{\Et}$. The finite filtration and its restrictions with projective stalks are assertions of the cited node, not an inference from a filtration with arbitrary lisse quotients.

source.place: Proof (1)–(2): ordered stratification and its finite extension filtration

proof.text: For each $q$, the stupid subcomplexes of [def-kun-truncations] give a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to\sigma_{\geq q+1}P\to\sigma_{\geq q}P\to P^q[-q]\to0$: in degree $q$ it is $0\to0\to P^q\xrightarrow{1}P^q\to0$, above $q$ it is $0\to P^i\xrightarrow{1}P^i\to0\to0$, and below $q$ it is zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] these sequences give distinguished triangles. Descending induction from $\sigma_{\geq b+1}P=0$ to $q=a$, using Step 5 and closure under shifts and cones, shows that $P=\sigma_{\geq a}P$ lies in $\mathcal H_{\Et}$. Closure under isomorphisms puts $K$ there. Together with Step 3 this proves the equality on the small étale site.

source.place: Proof, Step 1, the displayed stupid-truncation triangles and their finite induction

proof.text: Now pass to the small pro-étale convention of the statement. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] the comparison pullback $\nu_T^*$ is an equivalence on bounded constructible categories, for $T=X,U,\overline U$. It is exact on sheaves by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], hence triangulated on derived categories by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Both directions of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] identify the finite-Tor subcategories. The natural isomorphisms in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] and [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] identify the étale generators with the pro-étale generators; the latter applies because a closed immersion is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $j_!L$ is in degree zero. Indeed, by [def-weil-closed-immersion] the preimage of an affine $\Spec R$ under $g$ is $\Spec(R/I)$, which is quasi-compact; its diagonal is an isomorphism (a map factoring through a quotient $R/I$ is unique), hence quasi-compact. To see that all lisse coefficients on $U$ are included, use both directions of [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] and the stalk identification [lem-cbc-proetale-comparison-stalk]; the descended sheaf is lisse with the same finite flat stalks. Clause (3) of [det-sf-flat-model-generation], which is stated on either site, also gives thickness of the pro-étale finite-Tor category in its ambient derived category. Thus the relevant ambient thick closures remain inside the compared subcategories. A triangulated equivalence preserves shifts, triangles, isomorphisms and retract diagrams, and its inverse does so as well. It therefore carries the equality of Step 6 to the asserted equality in $D(X_{\Proet},A)$. The comparison natural transformations respect distinguished triangles, so the two-out-of-three isomorphism criterion [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] applies during this transport; and invertibility on the thick generators extends to the relevant closure by [lem-sf-generating-class-determination].

source.place: Unit proof, first paragraph: transport of immersion generators to the pro-étale convention

proof.text: For the constant-coefficient obstruction take $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_5$, $X=\mathbf G_m=\Spec k[t,t^{-1}]$ and $A=\mathbf F_3$ (the coefficient datum $\ell=3$, $E=\mathbf Q_3$, $n=1$). Consider the double cover $\pi:V=\Spec k[u,u^{-1}]\to X$, $t=u^2$. Its algebra is free of rank two with basis $1,u$, and it is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] applied to $Q(T)=T^2-t$, since $Q'=2u$ is invertible. The fibre of $\pi$ at a geometric generic point has two elements. By [thm-galois-fundamental] its permutation action gives a continuous character $\chi:\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)\to S_2\cong\{1,-1\}\subset\mathbf F_3^\times$. The finite-coefficient equivalence of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] realizes the one-dimensional sign representation as a lisse sheaf $L$ on $X$. Its local model is the free module $\mathbf F_3$, so $L$ is an allowed flat generator and belongs to $D^b_{ctf}$ by Step 3 with $j=g=1_X$.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: construction of the order-two Kummer local system

proof.text: Let $h:\eta=\Spec k(t)\to X$ be the generic-point map. Its exact inverse image on module sheaves is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so it induces a triangulated functor by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Use the exact equivalence [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules] to view its values as complexes of discrete $A[G]$-modules, $G=\operatorname{Gal}(k(t)^{\mathrm{sep}}/k(t))$. Define $\mathcal T$ to consist of complexes whose resulting cohomology is zero outside finitely many degrees and in each degree has a finite filtration with trivial one-dimensional $G$-quotients. This is a thick subcategory of the ambient derived category. Indeed intersection with a submodule and passage to the images of a filtration prove the submodule and quotient assertions (a subquotient of a trivial one-dimensional module is zero or that module); inverse images of a quotient's filtration concatenate with a submodule's filtration to prove closure under extensions. The long exact cohomology sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] then proves closure under triangles, since each middle cohomology is an extension of a quotient and a submodule of the adjacent cohomologies. The degree bound is the finite union of the two bounds with a shift. Shifts reindex the filtrations, and a retract gives a submodule on every cohomology group, proving closure under direct summands.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: the thick obstruction, with the filtration argument supplied

proof.text: Every constant-coefficient generator $Rg_*j_!A_U$ lies in $\mathcal T$. If its stratum omits $\eta$, its generic stalk is zero by the finite stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] for the closed immersion, which is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], and the vanishing assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]. If its stratum contains $\eta$, that locally closed subset is open dense in the integral $X$, its closure is $X$, and its restriction to $\eta$ is the constant $A$ with trivial $G$-action; these identifications are natural in the geometric point and hence $G$-equivariant. The derived generator is a sheaf by [lem-fin-closed-immersion]. Thus the thick closure of all constant-coefficient generators lies in $\mathcal T$. In contrast $h^*L$ is the nontrivial one-dimensional sign representation. To verify nontriviality, $t$ is not a square in $k(t)$: an equality $f(t)^2=tg(t)^2$ with coprime polynomials forces $t\mid f$ and then $t\mid g$, a contradiction. Hence $k(t)[u]/(u^2-t)$ is a separable quadratic field extension. By [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification] its two-element geometric fibre is a transitive $G$-set, so some element swaps the roots. Base-change compatibility in [thm-galois-fundamental] identifies this action with the restriction of $\chi$, giving the scalar $-1\ne1$ on $h^*L$. A one-dimensional nontrivial representation cannot have a filtration with trivial quotients. Therefore $L\notin\mathcal T$, and constant-coefficient generators do not generate $D^b_{ctf}$. Finally Step 7 transports both the constant generators and $L$ across the comparison equivalence, so the same failure holds in the pro-étale convention of the item.
